# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 12 LORNA COMES OVER

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

It was a chilly evening in October, with moon-drenched fog drifting across the harbor and winding like ribbons of silver through the seaward glens, when Lorna visited the house of dreams. Upon Hugh opening the door to her knock, she appeared to regret having come; however, Nell rushed past him, seized her, and pulled her inside.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0000 }

“I’m very happy that you chose this evening to visit,” she remarked cheerfully. “A large batch of especially delicious fudge was prepared by me earlier today, and an assistant is needed to consume it alongside us—in front of the fireplace—as we share tales. Captain Saul might also make an appearance. Today belongs to him.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0001 }

“No. Captain Saul is across at home,” Lorna replied. “He—he forced me to come here,” she appended, with a touch of defiance.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0002 }

“When I see him, I will express my gratitude to him for that,” Nell remarked, dragging comfortable armchairs in front of the hearth.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0003 }

“Oh, I do not mean that coming was something I did not wish to do,” Lorna objected, her face reddening slightly. “I—I have had thoughts of visiting—however, leaving is not always simple for me.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0004 }

“Naturally, parting from Mr. Vane must prove difficult for you,” Nell remarked pragmatically. It was her conclusion that referring to Rufus Vane as a settled reality now and then would be ideal, preventing the topic from acquiring unnecessary grimness through avoidance. Her judgment proved correct, since Lorna’s restrained demeanor instantly disappeared. It was clear she had been speculating about the extent of Nell’s awareness regarding her living circumstances, feeling unburdened when no clarifications proved necessary. Permitting her hat and coat to be removed, she settled with a youthful cuddle into the large armchair near Magog. Her attire was attractive and meticulous, featuring her usual accent of color via a red geranium placed at her pale neck. The glowing hearth fire made her lovely hair shimmer like liquid gold. Radiant with gentle amusement and charm were her ocean-blue eyes. Temporarily, affected by the small dwelling of dreams, she reverted to being a girl—one oblivious to previous times and their acrimony. Surrounding her completely was the climate of numerous affections that had hallowed the small dwelling; enveloping her was the camaraderie of two robust, contented, youthful individuals belonging to her own era; experiencing the enchantment of her environment, she surrendered to it—Miss Winifred and Captain Saul could hardly have identified her; Nell struggled to accept that this lively girl, who conversed and paid attention with the intensity of a deprived spirit, was the same chilly, distant female she had encountered on the beach. Furthermore, Lorna’s eyes gazed with immense longing at the bookstands situated between the windows!
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0005 }

“The collection of books we own is quite small,” Nell remarked, “yet each volume within it serves as a FRIEND. Over time, in various places, we have gathered our books, always refusing to purchase any volume before reading it beforehand and determining that it originated from the lineage of Joseph.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0006 }

Lorna let out a laugh, a lovely sound that appeared to resemble every bit of joy that had reverberated within the tiny home during the bygone times.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0007 }

“My father owned a small number of books, and I have them,” she remarked. “They have been read by me so often that I practically know them from memory. Books are rare for me to acquire. Though the Glen store contains a circulating library, the committee selecting books for Mr. Tibbs seems unaware of which ones belong to Joseph’s race, or maybe it does not matter to them. Because a book I truly enjoyed was such a rare find for me, I stopped procuring any.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0008 }

“I hope our bookshelves will be treated by you as your own,” Nell said.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0009 }

“You are completely and genuinely invited to borrow any book from them.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0010 }

“A banquet of rich offerings is being placed prior to my eyes by you,” Lorna uttered with delight. Subsequently, the chime of ten upon the clock caused her to stand up, somewhat reluctantly.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0011 }

“It is necessary for me to leave, as I failed to see how late it had gotten. Captain Saul frequently remarks that spending an hour does not require much time. However, I have remained for two—and oh, I truly have had a wonderful time,” she appended with candor.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0012 }

“Come often,” said Nell and Hugh. Having gotten up, they were standing side by side within the radiance of the hearth. Lorna gazed upon them—young, full of hope, joyful, embodying everything that she lacked and would permanently lack. The brightness faded from her countenance and eyes; the young girl disappeared; it was the grieving, betrayed woman who replied to the offer nearly coldly and departed with a pathetic speed.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0013 }

Nell observed her until she disappeared into the darkness of the cold and foggy night. Afterwards, she turned around deliberately toward the warmth of her own glowing hearthstone.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0014 }

“Is she not beautiful, Hugh? I am captivated by her hair. It extends down to her feet, according to Miss Winifred. Opal Pettigrew possessed lovely hair—however, Lorna’s possesses LIFE—each individual strand is animate gold.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0015 }

“She is extremely lovely,” Hugh concurred, with such genuine warmth that Nell nearly preferred him to display a WEE bit less fervor.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0016 }

“Hugh, if my hair was similar to Lorna’s, would it please you more?” she inquired yearningly.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0017 }

“For all the world, I would not change the color of your hair to anything other than what it currently is,” Hugh declared, offering a couple of persuasive gestures to match.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0018 }

Your hair wouldn't be golden—or any other shade, for that matter—if you were NELL”—
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0019 }

“Red,” Nell stated, her satisfaction dark.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0020 }

“Indeed, red—so it adds warmth to that milk-white skin and those gleaming gray-green eyes you have. Golden hair would not fit you in any way Queen Nell—MY Queen Nell—queen of my heart and life and home.”
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0021 }

“In that case, Lorna’s can be admired by you as much as you wish,” Nell stated generously.
{: #nw-v04-c12-p0022 }
